answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A ripple delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A meadow check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A velvet penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 11594 identities need 11594 bonds of 75 tokens, 2934 dollars of hardware and 14 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
